expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Prescott has some of the best weapons of any quarterback in football. The Cowboys were 2nd in the NFL in yards per game last season, so we shouldn't expect their offense to slow down this season, especially with how bad the defense looked in Week 1. Prescott has an elite track record against the Commanders (26, 23, 26, and 35 fantasy points in the last 4 games), and the Cowboys have one of the highest team totals on the board. This is my favorite game of the week to stack, so I want to be overweight on both of the quarterbacks.

players.notes: Elite weapons and a top implied team total against Washington.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I do not think the Cowboys defense is as bad as it looked Sunday night against the Giants, but there is very little hope, in my opinion, that they can fix their issues against running QBs in one week. Daniels should, at the very least, have a high floor because of the rushing.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Daniels never looked comfortable last week and had far too many drives stall out thanks to poor throws. However, he still finished the game with 18 fantasy points. If he can do that while playing poorly in a bad matchup, I can't wait to see what he does in a dream indoor matchup against the Cowboys. According to the NFL Pick Six show here on RotoGrinders, Dallas allowed the 4th-highest EPA per drive of any defense in any game since the start of last season. Daniels has rushing upside, weapons to work with, and a potentially favorable game script as a 3.5-point road underdog.

players.notes: Rushing floor and a high total in a great matchup.
Solid implied team total in a favorable home matchup.
Strong passing volume in a high-total home spot.
High rushing upside against a vulnerable defense.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: It's sort of shocking that the field isn't really running back to the Bears after a 59 point outburst last week, but I will take it. Ben Johnson continues to be adamant about scoring as many points as possible, and he's also generally going to be forced to do so given the fact that the Bears defense is absolutely putrid. Kevin O'Connell will be able to score points against the Bears, and Brian Flores' pressure packed defense is extremely susceptible to big plays while forcing you to the air often, as we saw last week. Ben Johnson should have answers to this Flores test, and that should mean a big Caleb game... again.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Williams was my favorite QB play last week and he is going to be another target of mine this week as we saw Caleb throw 2 passing TD’s while rushing for 2 more more.  I love pairing Caleb with Luther Burden, but he has quite a few weapons to target including Colston Loveland, who was the forgotten man in week 1.  Rome Odunze and D’Andrew Swift are other great options to pair with Caleb.  I will be at this game in Soldier Field so I will have a front row seat to watch Caleb and company put up elite offensive numbers once again.

players.notes: Multiple weapons available in a fast-paced game.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: This Green Bay offense is going to play a lot more through Jordan Love as long as Josh Jacobs is out. Love had a really good game against a tough Minnesota defense, and while the Jets looked better in Week 1, they were still a bad secondary last year.

players.notes: Increased pass volume with a strong team total.
Strong implied team total in a divisional matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Robinson has the ability to get 100 yards rushing and 100 yards receiving in this game. The Panthers were horrible at stopping the run and Robinson has such a great workload.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Robinson was a Core Play last week. I thought about untagging him after Cooper Rush was named the starter, but I held firm in my conviction. I'm glad I did, as Robinson turned 29 touches (including 8 receptions) into over 100 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. He draws a much better matchup this week, as the Panthers were absolutely shredded by the Bears' running backs in Week 1 (258 yards and 4 touchdowns). It's clear that Robinson doesn't have much competition for touches, and the Falcons will want to limit Rush as much as possible, which means a lot of carries and dump-offs for Robinson.

players.notes: Heavy workload with immense rushing and receiving upside.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: It's only one game, but I am ALL the way bought in new Ravens OC Declan Doyle. And that means big things for Derrick Henry, especially in a game where Zay Flowers is hurt (so is Ja'Kobi Lane). Jahmyr Gibbs wrecked this Saints defense in Week One, and Henry can do so too, especially with the significant uptick in outside zone runs called by Doyle.

players.notes: Heavy outside zone usage against a struggling run defense.
Elite touch volume in a high-implied-total offense.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Jones is a great value play at RB this weekend with Mason out of the game. The Bears' defense was horrible in Week 1, and with Carson Wentz starting, I expect the Vikings to feed Jefferson and run the ball.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Without Jordan Mason, Jones is simply mispriced. Yes, he's older, but Demond Claiborne is not ready for a real workload and Deejay Dallas is a career special teamer, and Jones is way too cheap given his pass catching and a matchup with the Bears defense.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Jones should be a true bell cow this week with Jordan Mason on IR. He’s priced as though he’s splitting the workload with Mason, and he has a seemingly great matchup.

players.notes: Clear Bell-cow workload with a great matchup against Chicago.
Strong rushing role as a home favorite against Tennessee.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Hall is checking in at around 10% projected ownership, which is far too low. He's coming off a solid fantasy season, despite playing in negative game scripts with bad quarterback play. He has a new quarterback (Geno Smith) and a new offensive coordinator (Frank Reich) this season. Based on his usage in Week 1, he still has his bell-cow role in this offense. He had 24 touches, a high success rate, and a high carry rate inside the 5-yard line. The Jets have one of the biggest o-line vs. d-line advantages this week, as the Packers are without some key players in their front seven (including Micah Parsons).

players.notes: Heavy Bell-cow touches and goal-line work.
Solid rushing share in a close divisional game.
Strong snap share and rushing role as a slight underdog.
Strong target volume and route participation.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I've seen this song and dance way too much as a Cowboys fan, but coming back home after that Sunday night loss, you want one of these Dallas WRs in your lineup. One of them is going to put up a big game. I'll lean Lamb, but either is in play here. It's just a great combination of a sense of urgency, Dak at home, and a matchup with a particular weakness they can exploit (Mike Sainristil).

players.notes: Great bounce-back spot exploiting a secondary weakness.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Brutal matchup but how many chances in your life will you get to play Ja'Marr Chase in a squeaky wheel spot where Zac Taylor said they need to scheme up touches for Chase at less than 25% projected ownership?

players.notes: Schemed touches and high target upside.
Strong target share and route volume.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: It only took one week and a concussion from Kyler Murray for me to go from a full fade on Jefferson to tagging him as a Core Play. That's all thanks to Carson Wentz and a matchup against the Bears. With Wentz under center, Jefferson has racked up a 32% target share in his career. He finally looked like the best receiver in football again, as he caught 8-of-9 targets for 92 yards and 2 touchdowns. He had a massive 48% air yards share and a 55% first-read rate in that game. The Vikings will likely be trailing in this one, and the Bears couldn't stop Bryce Young and Carolina's passing attack last week.

players.notes: Massive target and air yards share against a weak secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Ben Johnson should have answers to this Flores test, and I think that's going to be utilizing Burden's elite YAC ability to alleviate that pressure. Burden is one of the very best YAC players in the league, averaging the 4th most YAC per reception last season, and the 2nd year breakout candidate already picked up 29 yards of YAC in the opener. The Bears are going to continue to score gobs of points every week, and I think this week it sets up best for Burden.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Burden was a fairly popular play last week and he started out with an early fumble but did finish with 5 targets.  This offense is going to put up points and Burden isn’t projected to be as popular as he was last week.  His price tag is going to go up as the season goes on and I will continue targeting both he and Caleb Williams early and often this year.

players.notes: Elite yards after catch ability in a high-scoring offense.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Washington followed up his breakout last season with another dominant performance in Week 1 against the Browns, finishing with a 5/83/1 line on just 18 routes as the Jags rotated guys in during the 2nd half when the game was out of hand. He earned a target on 33% of his routes and posted an elite 4.61 yards per route run, continuing a near year long run as one of the most efficient and productive receivers in the entire league in one of the best offenses. The Broncos are a big step up in competition, but that should lead to significantly more routes, and he cooked this matchup last year (6/145/1 on 9 targets). It doesn't hurt that the Broncos defense looked very vulnerable against the Chiefs in Week One.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I usually don't love targeting players against the Broncos on a full slate, but everything sets up beautifully for Washington ($5,900 DK / $6,600 FD) this week. He was the best receiver on the Jaguars last season, and he got the WR1 treatment in Week 1 with 26% of the team's targets and 43% of the team's air yards. He runs about half of his routes from the slot, which is why I love him this week. The Broncos are extremely tough on outside receivers in large part thanks to Patrick Surtain. Trevor Lawrence looks like the real deal, Washington is his favorite target, and the slot is the way to attack the Broncos.

players.notes: Dominant slot route share and high target efficiency.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: DeVonta with a major letdown in Week 1, but Week 2 has a lot of promise for him. There's a chance the Titans secondary is not good at all. Omar Cooper had a 30-yard catch, Adonai Mitchell averaged 20 yards per reception, and Garrett Wilson went 6/79 against them in Week 1.

players.notes: Strong route participation and downfield target upside.
Strong route rate and red-zone usage.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Andrews has been tough to trust over the last couple of seasons, as he's lost playing time to Isaiah Likely. With Likely now in New York, Andrews appears to be back to a clear TE1. In Week 1, he ran a route on 70% of dropbacks. He could be the top receiving option this week, as Flowers has been ruled out. It's a great spot for all of the Ravens, as they are at home against the fast-paced Saints.

players.notes: Full route participation as the primary receiving option.
Elite route participation and seam target volume.
Strong seam and slot usage in an explosive offense.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Week 1 was a disappointment for people who rostered Mayer, but he is still a big threat at the position, and this salary on DraftKings is so much better than on FanDuel.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Mayer is too cheap on DraftKings, and he's in another good matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Mayer didn't have the huge fantasy outing that many of us were hoping for, but the Raiders let their foot off the gas in the second half of that blowout win over the Dolphins. The underlying usage for Mayer was solid, as he led the team in route participation, targets, and catches. This week's matchup against the Chargers is a more difficult one, but I actually view that as a positive, as the Raiders will be forced to air it out more. The best part is that Mayer will be much less-owned than he was in Week 1.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: I just want it on that record that if Mayer ends up being less owned than Dalton Schultz (which is what it looks like right now) he is a jam.

players.notes: Strong route participation and target volume against the Chargers.
Every-down route rate with strong red-zone involvement.
High route participation and seam upside.
Solid route rate and red-zone role.
